components.description: One semester of paid parental leave at full pay, relieving teaching, research and service, for a full-time tenured or tenure-track faculty member who becomes a parent (own or spouse's childbirth, or adoption of a pre-school-aged child) and will serve as the child's primary caregiver.
components.faculty_group_note: "a full-time faculty member who is tenured or tenure-track" (Faculty Manual Part VI ch. 4 sec. B)
components.eligible_parent_wording: "a full-time faculty member ... or that faculty member's spouse becomes the parent of a child, either by childbirth or by adoption of a pre- school-aged child"
components.caregiver_condition_wording: "for purposes of serving as the child's primary caregiver"; the written agreement includes "certification by the faculty member that the purpose of the leave will be to serve as the primary caregiver for that child during the period of leave"
components.dual_employee_rule: either one, but not both, may take this parental leave
components.entitlement_note: "shall, upon written request ... be entitled": the faculty member is entitled once the request is made; the written agreement records the arrangements (V2; schema 2c, a benefit the institution must grant once requested).
components.duration_note: One semester; a semester runs "from the first day of classes to the last day of examinations". Multiple births or simultaneous adoptions count as one leave event.
components.relief_note: Teaching, research and scholarship, and service ("including committee work and student advising") are each relieved for the semester. Where the leave semester would have carried more than half of the annual teaching load, the member "may be required to teach one additional course in another semester". Clinical duties are not named separately; the member "shall be relieved of his or her normal duties and responsibilities during the period of leave", so every duty is coded relieved.
components.use_limit_note: "may be used once per child and no more than three times during a faculty member's employment at Vanderbilt"; 'once per child' is a renewal with each birth, not a limit (U9). After three uses the member is entitled to FMLA or TMLA leave (unpaid) and, for short-term illness, paid medical leave ("Benefit Beyond Three Children").
components.time_window: during the semester in which the child is born or placed for adoption, or during any subsequent semester that begins no later than six months after the birth or adoption placement
components.notice: at least three (3) months' written notice (medical emergencies or adoption uncertainties excepted)
components.return_obligation: return to active status for at least an equivalent period immediately following the leave, to retain the benefits of the leave including salary paid, unless waived in writing by the provost

sequence.note: "Any parental leave taken under this policy shall be in addition to any leave granted because of medical incapacitation": for the birth parent the parental semester follows the medical leave for childbirth (it may also be taken in a later semester starting within six months of the birth; consecutive_after records the earliest placement the text allows). The link is ignored for the non-birth parent, for whom c2 does not count.

components.description: Federal FMLA: up to 12 weeks of unpaid, job-protected leave in a 12-month period for the birth, adoption or foster placement of a child (within 12 months of it), the employee's own serious health condition, or care of a seriously ill spouse; all FMLA purposes share the same 12 weeks.
components.faculty_group_note: "qualified employees, including faculty"; "a faculty member who has been employed at Vanderbilt for at least twelve (12) months"
components.eligible_parent_wording: "adoption, pregnancy, childbirth, or nursing an infant"; "to care for the faculty member's newborn child after birth or placement for adoption or foster care"; "Neither FMLA nor TMLA requires that the person taking leave for infant care be the primary caregiver."

components.entitlement_note: Statutory entitlement (29 U.S.C. 2612(a)(1): "shall be entitled"); the Manual's "may be entitled" refers to eligibility.

C, "a period of up to three (3) months"; the statute: "a total of 12 workweeks of leave during any 12-month period". Leave for own serious health condition and for care of a seriously ill spouse runs within the same 12 weeks ("run concurrently with, and are not in addition to"). Pay comes from the University's parental leave or short-term medical leave where they apply (c1, c3).
components.time_window: at any time during the first twelve (12) months following the date of birth or, in the case of adoption, custody of the child

notes: Governing document: the Faculty Manual snapshot of March 29, 2018 (2018_02), the 2017-18 edition, the nearest saved version to the reference date 2018-02-26; the version note accepts it as in force on that date (whether Part VI ch. 4 changed between the 11-14-2017 and 3-29-2018 snapshots is not verified). 2018_01 is the 2016-17 web edition of Part VI ch. 4 (snapshot 8/17/2016); its leave provisions match 2018_02 except that 2018_02 drops 'or declared domestic partner' / 'or domestic partner' from the parental, FMLA and TMLA eligibility wording, renumbers the chapter footnote [1], and adds to footnote [6] the FMLA eligibility sentence ('worked for the University for at least one year and for 1,250 hours ... newborn child after birth or placement for adoption or foster care'). Quotes are taken from 2018_02.

2018_00_link is the Human Resources (staff) Parental Leave policy, effective July 1, 2015 (Wayback capture 2019-08-25; no later revision date shown). It covers full-time staff and says 'Faculty and house staff should refer to their respective manuals for leave policies' (c14, excludes_main_faculty).

Birth parent chain: short-term medical leave for childbirth c2 (paid by c3, normally up to 6 weeks; up to six months with unusual complications) -> University parental leave c1, one semester at full pay ('in addition to any leave granted because of medical incapacitation'); FMLA c4 (12 weeks) and TMLA c5 (4 months) alongside from the start of c2. After three uses of parental leave: only FMLA/TMLA (unpaid) plus paid short-term illness.

Non-birth parent chain: University parental leave c1 (one semester at full pay, if the primary caregiver; only one spouse may take it), with FMLA c4 (12 weeks) and TMLA c5 (4 months) alongside from its start.

Parental leave c1 timing: it may be taken in the birth semester or any semester beginning within six months of the birth; c1 is linked consecutive_after the medical leave c2 (the 'in addition to' clause), which places it immediately after for the birth parent.

Medical leave for childbirth is coded as a leave (c2, U6) and its pay (c3, V1 childbirth benefit, 6 weeks), following rules V1 and V6, which cite this Vanderbilt provision. The six-month short-duration limit is c2's duration_max (complications); c3 keeps the childbirth period only (V6).

Schools of Medicine and Nursing parental leave (c10; the VUMC Faculty Parental Leave Policy per footnote [2]) is unit-limited (V3b): not counted. The Manual's footnote 17 says VUMC-employed faculty receive their benefits from VUMC.

Not components: scholarly leaves of absence (research purpose; a parent cannot take them for a birth); jury duty; military duty (USERRA); group life insurance, tuition benefits, accidental death insurance. 'Benefit Beyond Three Children' is recorded in c1's use_limit_note, c3 and c9.

Cited but not saved: the long-term disability summary plan description and plan documents (Part VI governs 'Any inconsistencies ... by the plan documents'); each college's and school's statement of leave principles (scholarly leave only); the Human Resources Policy definition of 'spouse' (tuition section). The TMLA text saved is the 2025 Code (history: amended 2005 and 2025); its terms (four months, 12 months full-time, three months' notice, unique-position exception) agree with the Manual's 2018 description, so statute_verified is set true on that basis.

TMLA: Tenn. Code Ann. 4-21-408(d)(2) limits it to employers with 100 or more full-time employees; the Manual applies it to Vanderbilt faculty. The statute says leave 'may be with or without pay at the discretion of the employer'; the Manual pays the short-term illness part.

Calendar: semesters (parental leave by semester; 'each semester shall run from the first day of classes to the last day of examinations'), no length stated: calendar.kind = semester, and the term length follows R8's order.
